newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Liberty rises on bullish investor meeting.
newsitem.headline: Liberty rises on bullish investor meeting.

text.p: Shares in South African insurance and financial services giant Liberty Life rose to a three-month high at the start of trade on Wednesday, lifted by a bullish presentation to investors late on Tuesday, dealers said.
However Liberty's move up to 132 rand, a gain of 225 cents or nearly two percent by 0800 GMT, was seen short-lived, dealers said.
"At the presentation Liberty management gave reasons why their shares were underpriced," a dealer said.
"Although it was a very bullish presentation, the returns on their portfolios to shareholders have lagged other companies and until they improve that, any confidence is going to be short-lived."
Volumes in Liberty Life Association of Africa Ltd shares were thin at 25,300, but the stock was one of the most active on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.

But stocks in subsidiary Liberty Strategic Investments Ltd (Libsil), the Liberty Life subsidiary which holds the group's major investments in blue-chip South African firms, dipped 15 cents to 16.75 rand after a stronger start.

Roy McAlpine, head of the asset management firm in the Liberty Life stable, told investors that Libsil's assets, which include stakes in brewing giant South African Breweries and Standard Bank Investment Corp, were not cast in stone.
"(Libsil's) discount to net asset value in recent years vacillated between 10 and 20 percent...It is quite within our power to unlock the discount at any time," McAlpine said.
